memory_candidates.content: This repo's headless 'Sync all' deploy path (sync.scan_all_artifacts, used by deploy-headless.sh and the <leader>al 'Load Core'/'Sync all' picker option) does NOT recurse into scripts/tests/ or scripts/lib/ subdirectories for the scripts category at all -- confirmed empirically via a headless-nvim probe returning zero is_subdir=true entries for that category, across BOTH already-deployed and brand-new subdirectory scripts. This is broader than the previously-documented 'brand-new file' gap in source-store-deploy-boundary.md. The reliable one-off workaround: invoke `loader.copy_scripts(manifest, source_dir, target_dir, protected_paths)` directly via `nvim --headless -c "luafile <script>" -c "qa!"`, requiring `package.path` extended with the repo's `lua/?.lua;lua/?/init.lua`, `require("neotex.plugins.ai.shared.extensions.manifest").read(source_dir)` to load the manifest, and `require("neotex.plugins.ai.shared.extensions.loader")` for copy_scripts and load_syncprotect. This primitive correctly handles subdirectory entries (it iterates manifest.provides.scripts literally, so 'tests/foo.sh' style entries copy correctly with parent-dir creation and .sh permission preservation) where the incremental scan path does not.

When a plan's verification bar says 'grep for pattern X returns zero hits' but the very artifact the plan builds (a canonical writer script) legitimately CONTAINS pattern X as its own sanctioned internal implementation, the literal grep will never return zero once the plan's own work is done -- the correct reading is 'zero hits outside the canonical writer,' which is usually stated correctly in the plan's own Goal/Overview prose ('X is the only writer') even when a later verification bullet inherited unqualified wording. Don't treat this as a defect to chase; verify the qualified claim (zero hits outside the sanctioned location), record the literal grep's real count as a reported finding, and move on -- re-deriving live numbers and reporting where they diverge from the plan's literal text is the correct behavior, not silently 'fixing' the grep result to match stale wording.
